Routing.//: Every module serves /api/v1/{module}. The mobile client's base URL is https://api.diaspora.app/v1, so it addresses /v1/{module}. EnablePrefixCompatibility rewrites the second onto the first before routing, for every module identically. Set it to false on a deployment whose ingress already rewrites; the canonical prefix is then the only one served. Watch diaspora.api.compatibility_rewrites to find out whether anything still uses the alias.

Notifications.//: The Communication Platform. Every value here has a working default in code; the section exists so a deployment can see what it may change without reading the source.

Realtime.//InstanceCount: How many copies of this application the deployment runs. Nothing can detect this at runtime, and a value above 1 with no backplane means live delivery reaches only the members attached to each instance — so the host refuses to start on that combination rather than failing silently, one member at a time.
Realtime.//EnableDetailedErrors: Off outside local development: a hub exception message can carry an identifier or a member's own data, and it reaches a device the platform does not control.

Backplane.//: What carries fan-out between instances. 'None' is single-instance and is the shipped position. Any other value declares that an adapter has been installed beneath the hub; that adapter reads its own connection settings, and no credential for it belongs in this file.

Push.//: The push transport. 'None' ships: the whole delivery path runs and the attempt is recorded as unsupported, so acquiring a provider is a registration rather than a rewrite. 'Loopback' reports success without sending, for local development only — the host refuses it outside Development and Testing.
Push.//credentials: No credential is committed here and none should be. CredentialsPath points at a secret the orchestrator mounts; CredentialsJson exists for a platform with no filesystem to mount into and must arrive from a secret store. Setting both is a startup error, because the one actually used then depends on which the adapter reads first.
Push.//Settings: Free key/value pairs an adapter reads and this module never does. A Firebase Cloud Messaging adapter, for example, is configured entirely by Provider='Firebase', ProjectId, CredentialsPath and any keys it documents here — no vendor name appears anywhere in the platform's own code.

Notifications.//UnsubscribeSigningKey: B13.3. Signs the one-category unsubscribe token in an email footer, which is redeemed with no session behind it. Empty means a key is generated at startup: links then stop working on restart and are refused by any other instance, so a deployment that sends email must supply one from its secret store. It is not a credential for anybody else's service — a leaked one lets somebody unsubscribe any member from any category, which is a denial of notifications rather than a disclosure.
Notifications.//UnsubscribeLinkLifetimeDays: Ninety days. The member this link exists for is the one who has stopped opening the app, so a link that expired in a week would be dead in exactly the mailbox it was meant for.

Sms.//: Outbound SMS, which is how every one-time code reaches a member. Inert as shipped: with no DefaultProvider and no credentials the adapter does not register at all, and the logging placeholder stays behind IOtpDeliveryService. That placeholder now reports failure rather than pretending, so a deployed host in this state will tell a member their code could not be sent instead of leaving them waiting.
Sms.//DefaultProvider: Twilio or AfricasTalking. Carries every destination no route claims — on a platform for people living abroad, that is most of the world. Required once anything else here is set.
Sms.//Routes: Destinations routed away from the default, matched longest-prefix so +1876 can be treated differently from +1. Ships empty on purpose: a country list is a claim about a provider's coverage that this repository cannot verify and that changes without notice, and a wrong entry sends a member's sign-in code to a gateway that will not carry it. Copy the example below and check it against the countries actually enabled on your account.
Sms.//FallBackToDefaultProvider: Whether a destination whose routed provider is failing may go out on the default one instead. Only ever applied to a transient failure — a number the first provider rejected as invalid is invalid on the second wire too.
Sms.//TimeoutSeconds: Per attempt. The retry budget belongs to the operational policy catalogue, not here.

Twilio.//: Secrets. Supply through the environment or the secret store, never this file.
Twilio.//From: A sending number in E.164, or a Messaging Service SID beginning MG. The Messaging Service is the better answer for a global app: it holds a pool of numbers and picks one appropriate to the destination, which is the difference between a UK member seeing a local number and seeing an American one they will not trust.

AfricasTalking.//: Secrets. Supply through the environment or the secret store, never this file.
AfricasTalking.//SenderId: A registered alphanumeric sender id or short code. Optional — without one the account default is used, which on a sandbox account is the only thing that works.
AfricasTalking.//UseSandbox: The sandbox also only accepts the literal username 'sandbox'. Setting one without the other gives an authentication failure that reads like a bad key.

Payments.//: Payout rails. Inert as shipped: an adapter with no credentials is not registered at all, and PayoutProviderRouter then refuses with financial.payout.provider_not_registered rather than producing a 401 on somebody's withdrawal. Fill these in from user-secrets or a vault, never here — this file is committed.
Payments.//_webhooks: Payout callbacks arrive at POST /api/v1/financial/webhooks/{provider}/payouts — a different route from the payment one, so an endpoint can be configured to receive only payout events. A callback is one of two ways a withdrawal settles; the resolution sweep is the other, and neither is allowed to be the only one.
Payments.//_enabling: Supplying credentials enables NO corridor by itself. Which countries, rails and currencies an account may actually serve is Financial:PayoutRouting, and every row there stays Unknown — and refuses — until somebody confirms it against the provider's own documentation. See docs/financial/payout-routing.md.

Stripe.//: Stripe Connect transfers to connected accounts, plus connected-account onboarding state.
Stripe.//SecretKey: sk_test_... or sk_live_.... REPLACE_ME via: dotnet user-secrets set "Payments:Stripe:SecretKey" "sk_test_..." --project src/Diaspora.Api
Stripe.//Provider: The name the capability matrix must use for this adapter.
Stripe.//ApiVersion: Pinned deliberately. Raising it is a code change with a test run behind it.
Stripe.//WebhookSecret: whsec_.... A DIFFERENT secret from SecretKey, issued per endpoint. REPLACE_ME via user-secrets. Without it payout callbacks are refused rather than trusted — an unconfigured deployment cannot tell a Stripe callback from anybody's POST.
Stripe.//WebhookToleranceSeconds: How far from now a callback's timestamp may be. A correctly signed callback stays correctly signed for ever, so this is what makes the signature mean anything about freshness.

PayPal.//: PayPal Payouts. Authenticates a client id and secret pair for an access token rather than presenting a key per request, so both are required.
PayPal.//ClientId: REPLACE_ME. The REST app's client id.
PayPal.//ClientSecret: REPLACE_ME via: dotnet user-secrets set "Payments:PayPal:ClientSecret" "..." --project src/Diaspora.Api
PayPal.//ApiBase: Sandbox by default and deliberately so: a deployment that has not thought about which environment it is in should not be in the one that moves real money. Live is https://api-m.paypal.com.

Flutterwave.//: Flutterwave v3 transfers. A payout destination's provider token must be recorded as 'bankCode:accountNumber'; any other shape is refused rather than guessed at.
Flutterwave.//SecretKey: FLWSECK_TEST-... or FLWSECK-.... REPLACE_ME via: dotnet user-secrets set "Payments:Flutterwave:SecretKey" "..." --project src/Diaspora.Api
Flutterwave.//DebitCurrency: The currency the platform's own Flutterwave balance is denominated in. Empty lets the account default apply.
Flutterwave.//WebhookSecretHash: The secret hash Flutterwave echoes in the verif-hash header, set on their dashboard. REPLACE_ME via user-secrets. This is a shared secret rather than a signature over the body, so it proves the sender knows it and nothing about the payload — terminate these on TLS you control.

RateLimiting.//Authenticated: Application traffic on the module groups that ask to be throttled (Trust, Conversations, Bookmarks). Not a credential-exchange budget: those endpoints are already behind authorisation, and this is here so a runaway client cannot drive unbounded load. It partitions on the client address, because the limiter deliberately runs before authentication — which makes ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies load-bearing on any deployment behind an ingress.

ForwardedHeaders.//: KnownProxies must list the load balancer / ingress addresses in each deployed environment. Empty here means forwarded headers are ignored, which is the safe default: better to see the proxy address than to trust a spoofable X-Forwarded-For from an unknown source.
